messages:
sarah: Heads up — overnight perf job shows ~18% regression in cross-node throughput for the 4xTP pipeline profile on EFA cluster. nvlink clusters look fine. attaching quick profiler excerpt.

jon: Yeah saw that too when I spun up the same bench. latency tail pushed up around the all-reduce phases.

maria: Can you paste the relevant profiler slice + counters? curious if this is more comm or compute.

sarah: Paste from `perf-slice` (trimmed):
```
[timeline] step 42: compute 12.4ms | wait_comm 9.8ms | allreduce 11.6ms
[net] efa_sent 1.9GB | efa_qdepth 64 -> spikes to 256 during allreduce
[kvcache] miss_rate 7.3% -> jump to 21% at same time
[kernel] selected GEMM=v2_small_seq for seq=64 on CPU fallback (unoptimized)
```
Notice KV cache miss spike co-occurs with increased allreduce counts.

sasha: Interesting — KV cache thrash causing extra small allreduces (more frequent kv syncs) could expose EFA qdepth/backpressure, unlike NVLink where intra-node transfers hide it.

jon: I also captured `nvprof` equivalent on an nvlink run: allreduce overlapped with compute much more (wait_comm ~3ms). On EFA it's serialized.

maria: Two hypotheses: 1) kernel selector is falling back to unoptimized path for small seq/thread combos when fabric latency increases -> longer compute and mis-timed comm. 2) batching heuristics produce bigger micro-batch bursts across devices causing simultaneous allreduces and saturating NIC qdepth.

sarah: Agreed. Quick experiment: I bumped batching_window_ms 5->8 and reduced per-device max_batch_tokens by 10% on the nightly job. That reduced simultaneous allreduce peaks (efa_qdepth spike went from 256->110) and throughput recovered ~9%.

perf-bot: @sarah next run scheduled: jobs/ci/perf/2087654321/retry-1 (ETA 18m) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

jon: We should probably change two things: tweak kernel selection heuristic to prefer the optimized GEMM variant when net latency > X (i.e., favor compute-heavy kernels that better hide comm), and add a randomized micro-batch staggers across TP ranks (stagger by 1 micro-step) to spread allreduce windows.

sasha: Also add a KV cache stabilization: if miss_rate > 10% for two consecutive steps, throttle new KV inserts for 1 step (gives highway to catch up). That would reduce churn.

maria: For kernel selector: propose a small cost model tweak: cost = compute_ms + alpha * net_lat_ms. Increase alpha when fabric==EFA or when measured p95_net_latency>threshold. Simple win without heavy refactor.

sarah: I ran a microbenchmark with alpha x2 on EFA nodes: selected optimized GEMM even for small seqs -> allreduce wait dropped ~30% for those steps. Will send results after perf-bot finishes.

jon: Ops action: can infra add EFA qdepth telemetry to the per-cluster dashboards? current metrics too aggregated.

infra-bot: New monitor created: cluster/efa/qdepth (granularity 1s) by @jon :white_check_mark:

sasha: Action items:
- sarah: post perf traces from retry-1 + the alpha tweak run (upload to perf bucket)
- maria: spec for kernel selector cost param + unit test cases
- jon: add stagger scheduling option to runtime (config flag) + rollout on canary
- infra: keep qdepth monitor and alert if sustained > 200 for >30s

sarah: I'll also open a small PR to reduce default batching_window_ms from 6->5 on EFA profiles until we have heuristics in.

maria: Sounds good. if perf-bot pass we can iterate mid-week and aim to ship heuristics before next release. :thumbsup:

sarah: thanks all — will post the perf traces here when available.

perf-bot: Retry-1 completed: throughput +10% vs failing job, tail latency improved. details: https://perf.internal/runs/2087654321/retry-1

jon: Nice. please merge the monitor + small config changes as hotfix.

sasha: I created a short doc draft on the scheduling staggers and KV backoff heuristics under /docs/runtime/comm-mitigation (link in thread). :paperclip:

sarah: PRs opened: runtime#3421 (stagger), selector#117 (alpha param), infra#78 (qdepth dash). Assigning reviewers.

maria: Thanks — will review selector changes this afternoon.

sarah: closing for now, will follow up with detailed traces. :rocket:
